question: Which institute of Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) developed India’s first genome-edited rice variety DRR Rice 100 (Kamla)?

options.text: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research, Hyderabad
ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi
ICAR-Central Institute of Agricultural Engineering, Bhopal

solution:
The correct answer is __**ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research, Hyderabad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India’s first genome-edited rice variety DRR Rice 100 (Kamla)** was developed by the **ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR), Hyderabad**. This institute is a renowned research center specializing in rice improvement and cultivation.
 
• The development of DRR Rice 100 (Kamla) marks a significant step forward in agricultural biotechnology in India. This genome-edited rice variety was created using the **CRISPR/Cas9 genome-editing technology**, a cutting-edge tool that allows precise genetic modifications.
 
• The rice variety was developed to enhance certain desirable traits such as **higher yield, pest resistance, and better grain quality**. Genome editing allows scientists to introduce specific changes in the DNA without introducing foreign genes.
 
• ICAR-IIRR plays a pivotal role in **rice research, development, and dissemination of improved rice varieties**. Their efforts have consistently contributed to increasing rice productivity and ensuring food security in India.
 
• Genome-edited crops like DRR Rice 100 are distinct from genetically modified organisms (GMOs) because they do not involve the transfer of foreign genes, making them more acceptable in terms of regulatory frameworks and public opinion.
 
• The rice variety was named **Kamla** to signify its importance as a milestone in Indian agricultural research and its contribution to ensuring food security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research, Hyderabad:**

 
 
• The **ICAR-IIRR** is located in Hyderabad, Telangana, and is dedicated to rice research and development.
 
• It focuses on **developing high-yielding, pest-resistant, and climate-resilient rice varieties**.
 
• It is involved in advanced agricultural technologies like genome editing and hybrid rice breeding.
 
• The institute contributes to ensuring food security in India, where rice is a staple food for a majority of the population.
 
 
 
• **Genome Editing in Agriculture:**
 
 
• **Genome editing** refers to the use of technologies like CRISPR/Cas9 to make precise modifications in an organism’s DNA.
 
• Unlike GMOs, genome-edited crops do not involve the insertion of foreign DNA, making them more acceptable in regulatory frameworks.
 
• Applications of genome editing include improving **crop yield, pest resistance, and drought tolerance**, and enhancing nutritional content.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Options:**
 
 
• **Option 1 (Correct): ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research, Hyderabad** – The institute developed DRR Rice 100 using CRISPR/Cas9 technology.
 
• **Option 2: ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi** – While this is one of India’s premier agricultural research organizations, it was not involved in the development of DRR Rice 100.
 
• **Option 3: ICAR-Central Institute of Agricultural Engineering, Bhopal** – This institute focuses on agricultural engineering and mechanization, not crop breeding or genome editing.
 
• **Option 4: ICAR-National Rice Research Institute (NRRI), Cuttack** – Although NRRI is a leading research center for rice, DRR Rice 100 was not developed here.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of DRR Rice 100:**

 
 
• DRR Rice 100 demonstrates the potential of genome editing in addressing agricultural challenges.
 
• The variety can contribute to reducing **input costs** for farmers by lowering the need for pesticides and fertilizers due to its pest resistance and enhanced traits.
 
• It aligns with India’s goals of ensuring **sustainable agriculture and food security**.
 
 
 
• **CRISPR/Cas9 Technology:**
 
 
• This genome-editing tool enables precise changes in DNA, allowing targeted improvement in traits such as yield and resistance.
 
• It is faster and more accurate than traditional breeding methods.
 
• CRISPR-edited crops are gaining global attention for their potential in **revolutionizing agriculture**.
